title: Commit phasing and usage-velocity credits architecture
creator: Avery Chen
description: Design a repeatable pricing architecture that combines phased commit bands with a Usage Velocity Index (UVI) and escrowed prepay credits to both (1) reduce sticker shock in multi-year agreements and (2) preserve revenue capture on rapid expansion. This ticket defines the model, anti-abuse guardrails, operational hooks (billing/contract/console), and a pilot plan for mid-market and strategic accounts.
acceptance_criteria: Detailed UVI formula documented and validated with historical usage (sheet + sample calculation)
Billing contract template updated to support escrowed credits and phased true-up language and approved by Legal
Implementation plan with required billing integrations, invoice flow, and UI hooks (Console + Account page)
Pilot runbook for 10 accounts with expected financial model and rollback criteria
Dashboard queries for UVI, credit balances, true-up amounts, and revenue leakage detection instrumented in Datadog/Looker
success_metrics: Increase multi-year renewal conversion by +6 percentage points in pilot cohort vs control
Reduce mid-year revenue recognition variance due to expansion by >= 40% (pilot cohort)
< 1% of contracts show anomalous UVI changes flagged as potential abuse
Average time-to-agree on renewal proposals reduced by 20% for piloted accounts
proposed_solution: Core components: 1) Commit phasing: allow customers to lock a baseline commit with optional year-over-year acceleration bands (example: Year1 70%, Year2 85%, Year3 100% of forecasted baseline). 2) Usage Velocity Index (UVI): a normalized 90-day rolling usage velocity metric used to set uplift-trigger thresholds. UVI = (MAvg30 * 3 + P90)/4 normalized to cohort baseline. 3) Escrowed prepay credits: customers can prepay a tranche for future burst capacity; credits are held in an escrow balance and consumed before overage billing. Credits decay only on contract reductions per contract schedule (e.g., 25% unlock per year) to avoid cliff refunds. 4) True-up flow: quarterly automated true-ups that apply escrow credits first, then invoice net overage; late true-ups trigger a configurable finance hold. 5) Guardrails: minimum effective ARPU floor by account tier, anti-abuse velocity caps, and automated anomalous-velocity alerts that pause credit consumption pending review. 6) Billing/Legal hooks: standard contract clauses (appendix) and invoice line items to make credit flows auditable. Implementation notes: store UVI and credit balances in billing ledger; expose UVI trend and projected true-up estimate in Console account view; add flags for Pilot-eligible accounts.
tradeoffs: Lower near-term cash collection if credits reduce immediate overage invoicing vs better renewals conversion — tradeoff favors ARR expansion retention for enterprise deals
Increased billing complexity: requires ledger changes and audit trails; mitigated by small pilot and limited rollout
More manual Legal review initially for non-standard escrow clauses — will template after pilot
Risk of gaming velocity metric by synthetic traffic; mitigations include velocity caps, anomaly detection, and contract terms
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (Design, Feb): finalize UVI formula, build sample models for top 50 ARR accounts, draft contract appendix
Phase 1 (Pilot, Mar-Apr): enable for 10 pilot accounts (sales-nominated) with account teams trained; monitor UVI, credit consumption, and true-up accuracy weekly
Phase 2 (Iterate, May): incorporate pilot feedback, finalize templates, update billing integrations and Console UX
Phase 3 (Gradual rollout, Jun-Jul): open to mid-market cohort, expose opt-in in Console; provide pricing playbook to AE/CS
Rollback criteria: if pilot shows >10% unexpected revenue leakage or >2 flagged abuse incidents, pause credit consumption and revert to standard true-up invoicing
notes: Sales feedback 2025-02-20: AEs like the predictable spend window but requested a visual estimator in the quote wizard
Finance feedback 2025-02-25: require GL mapping for escrow movements; want quarterly netting detail on invoices
Legal feedback 2025-02-27: accept escrow clause with limited release schedule but require stronger anti-abuse language
Design feedback 2025-02-28: Console UX should show projected true-up and credit consumption with an 'explain' tooltip
